growth.title: From a seed to a new life
growth.text: Follow a corn seedling through the five stages of our process and on into your garden. Choose a stage to see it.
growth.canvasLabel: 3D model of a corn seedling in its cell, at the selected stage

stages.name: Sowing
stages.text: The corn seed goes two to three centimetres deep into moist substrate inside its cell, and the batch is logged.

stages.name: Germination
stages.text: In the chamber, at 20 to 30 °C with 12 to 14 hours of light, corn reached one hundred percent germination in our trial.

stages.name: Early growth
stages.text: On the growing shelf, under supplementary light and kept moist but never waterlogged, the first leaves appear.

stages.name: Hardening off
stages.text: The seedling is moved outdoors bit by bit so its tissue toughens and it reaches transplant without stress.

stages.name: Ready for your garden
stages.text: With two or three true leaves and twelve to eighteen centimetres tall, it is labelled with its batch and dispatched.

stages.name: In your garden
stages.text: Planted with its cell, the corn keeps growing in your garden until it forms its stalk, leaves and ears.

products.title: Seedlings ready to transplant
products.intro: A GREENOVA seedling is germinated in a biodegradable cell, with formed roots and developed true leaves, and hardened off for outdoor conditions.

tomatoNote.title: Why tomato has its own protocol
tomatoNote.text: In the first trial, tomato reached 37.5% at 72 hours. That wasn't a failure: the species takes five to eight days to germinate, and we measured too early. The improvement plan came out of that reading.
items: Evaluate each batch for at least eight days before discarding seed.
Keep the chamber between 25 and 28 °C during germination.
Pre-germinate on damp paper for the 24 hours before sowing.
Use certified seed with a recent packing date.

process.title: Five stages, one protocol per species
process.intro: Every batch follows the same sequence. What changes between corn, cucumber and tomato is depth, temperature, light and watering.

stages.name: Sowing and logging
stages.text: Seed selection, moistened substrate, filling the cells and sowing at each species' depth: corn at 2 to 3 cm, cucumber at 1 to 2 cm, tomato at half a centimetre. The batch is logged.
stages.alt: Cell trays with substrate in front of the chamber

stages.name: Germination in the chamber
stages.text: 20 to 30 °C for corn, 25 to 30 °C for cucumber and 22 to 28 °C for tomato. The sensors log each batch's conditions to the microSD card.
stages.alt: Seedlings germinating inside the chamber with sensors

stages.name: Early growth
stages.text: A growing shelf with supplementary light, watering tailored to each species and a daily health check.
stages.alt: Corn seedlings growing under LED lamps

stages.name: Hardening off
stages.text: Gradual exposure to outdoor conditions to toughen the tissue and reduce transplant stress.
stages.alt: Trays of seedlings outdoors while hardening off

stages.name: Selection and dispatch
stages.text: Weak seedlings are discarded; the rest are labelled for traceability, grouped by format and dispatched.

process.loss: We expect a ten percent loss between seedlings discarded as weak and health losses.
process.waste: Substrate waste and discarded plant material are composted at the school. We use no restricted crop-protection products.

projects.title: What we have already done
projects.intro: GREENOVA didn't start as a business plan. It started with a hand-built chamber and a trial that taught us to read our data carefully.

items.name: Building the chamber
items.text: On an adapted glass container we fitted the Arduino board, the LED grow light, the ventilation and the sensors. The team soldered, wired and calibrated every module in the school lab.

items.name: The first germination trial
items.text: Corn and cucumber reached one hundred percent at 48 hours. Tomato reached 37.5% at 72 hours; the analysis showed we had measured before its natural cycle ended, which led to the protocol per species.

items.name: The Pedro Pablo Sánchez school garden
items.text: Our seedlings were transplanted into the school's garden, where the team prepared the ground, planted and watered.

items.name: The latest chamber upgrade
items.text: The current version adds a second chamber and more lamps, with room for eight twelve-cell trays per batch.

about.title: A company born in the lab
about.intro: GREENOVA is a student-run company at Escuela Secundaria Pedro Pablo Sánchez in La Chorrera, Panama Oeste. We grow and sell corn, cucumber and tomato seedlings germinated under controlled conditions.

story.title: From science project to company
text: Urban gardening is growing in Panama because fresh vegetables keep getting more expensive. Yet most people who want to grow their own fail at the very first step: getting the seed to germinate.
We built an automated chamber to take that uncertainty away. Once the data showed it worked, in 2026 we wrote the business plan to turn the prototype into a production unit.

mission.title: Mission
mission.text: To grow and offer high-quality seedlings using automation that ensures the right conditions for germination and growth, promoting accessible, sustainable and innovative gardening for homes, schools and small growers in Panama Oeste.

vision.title: Vision
vision.text: By 2029, to be a benchmark student-run company in the province, known for the quality of its products, its innovation and its contribution to environmental education and urban growing.

items.q: What exactly is a GREENOVA seedling?
items.a: A seedling germinated in a biodegradable fibre cell, with formed roots and developed true leaves, hardened off for outdoor conditions. It arrives ready to transplant.

items.q: Which species do you sell and when are they ready?
items.a: Corn, cucumber and tomato. Corn is delivered 10 to 14 days after sowing, cucumber at 12 to 18 days and tomato at 25 to 35 days.
Plant the biodegradable cell whole, without pulling the seedling out. That avoids root damage, the main reason home transplants fail. Every purchase includes a short guide.

items.q: What if the seedling doesn't take?
items.a: If it fails to take within three days of transplanting, we replace it free of charge when you show its traceability label.
The species, batch code, sowing date, age in days and care tips.
At the pick-up stand at Escuela Secundaria Pedro Pablo Sánchez during breaks and after classes, through the form on this site, or via social media and messaging.
We arrange deliveries within a ten-kilometre radius. Institutional orders of five trays or more are delivered directly at no extra cost.

items.q: How far ahead should a school garden order?
items.a: Scheduled orders for institutions reserve production two weeks in advance.
